findings.claim: The row's sole rear-seam driver is carried entirely by the WEB rendering of the seam verse: no oshb ref or pointed splice stands at Isa.66.18, and the English run the row quotes supplies a verb the MT does not have.
findings.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs lists web:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18 with no oshb counterpart, and the warrant reads that 66:18 'opens with a first-person emphatic pivot' evidenced only by “For I know their works and their thoughts.” (web:Isa.66.18). MT 66:18 opens "וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier): no verb governs 'their works and their thoughts' -- "בָּאָ֕ה" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier) is the 3fs predicate of the gathering clause that follows -- so WEB's 'know' is a translator's supply and WEB's 'For' renders the waw of "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier). The pivot claim is nonetheless byte-true, since "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" is the verse-initial emphatic 1cs independent pronoun, so the seam itself survives re-derivation; only the shipped warrant is translation-dependent. Tier-4/engagement-class defect, not a byte-false claim.
findings.proposed_change: Add "oshb:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18" to boundary_evidence_refs and carry the pivot on a pointed splice of the verse-initial "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" at byte tier, retaining the WEB run as rendering only. No span change.

findings.claim: The front-seam onset run the row splices itself opens with a backward-linking connective, a byte-true continuity signal across the row's own Isa.66.14|Isa.66.15 seam that the row neither discloses nor rebuts.
findings.grounds: MT 66:15 opens "כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier); the leading "כִּֽי" subordinates the theophany announcement to the immediately preceding clause "וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו" (oshb:Isa.66.14, byte tier), and 66:16 chains a second connective of the same form, "כִּ֤י בָאֵשׁ֙" (oshb:Isa.66.16, byte tier). The row splices the connective inside its onset run and glosses it 'for behold', then argues the run purely as an onset; the continuity force of the connective at the row's own front seam is never disclosed, which the cross-seam cohesion rule requires. The seam is still defensible on the presentative and the subject/register change, so no merge is proposed.
findings.proposed_change: Add a one-clause disclosure to device_notes or strongest_rejected_alternative acknowledging the backward force of the connective opening 66:15 and stating why the presentative onset and the subject shift override it. No span change.

findings.claim: confidence 'high' does not survive the row's own evidence.
findings.grounds: The rear seam carries no original-language evidence at the seam verse and the front seam carries an undisclosed byte-level continuity signal, both under a 'high' band; the neighbour row spanning Isa.66.12-Isa.66.14 carries the identical Isa.66.14|Isa.66.15 seam on the same theophany-onset driver at 'medium'. The row's own span is not a whole chapter, so the chapter-fallback cap is not what is at issue -- the band simply outruns the warrants as shipped.
findings.proposed_change: Reduce confidence to 'medium'. Dependent on the two seam-warrant remedies above: if both are repaired, the band may be re-opened rather than fixed at medium.

findings.grounds: The parenthetical reads "(web:Isa.66.17, 'says Yahweh'; this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed below)"; 'disclosed below' is a positional reference to a later field of the row's own serialization, which the register-purge rule bars. The disclosure it points at is itself correct -- the inventory records exactly one ketiv/qere note at MT 66:17, single-witness, and the row takes no position on the reading.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'disclosed below' with a self-contained clause, e.g. "(web:Isa.66.17, 'says Yahweh'; the verse is ketiv/qere-bearing, single-witness, and the row takes no position on the reading)".

findings.claim: The couplet's stated cohesion warrant does not bind Isa.66.23 to Isa.66.24 against the verse-final closure-class signal the row itself computes at 66:23, and the closure test the neighbouring row applies is satisfied at this internal juncture but never run.
findings.grounds: The row gives two reasons for holding the couplet: that 'it is the book's terminal span (no rear seam follows 66:24)' -- a tiling fact, not a cohesion signal -- and that the couplet's internal turn 'is a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it', which distinguishes the couplet from what precedes rather than binding its two verses to each other. Against them: MT 66:23 closes on "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier), re-swept as verse-final in exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier; Isa.39.6, Isa.54.1, Isa.65.25, Isa.66.21, Isa.66.23, word-bound at all five) -- the row's own digit, confirmed; and MT 66:24 opens on a fresh scene with a new subject and setting, "וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier). The neighbouring row spanning Isa.66.18-Isa.66.22 rejects a seam at a verse-final speech signature only because 'no addressee, frame, or scene shift of its own' accompanies it; that test's second limb is met at 66:23|66:24, and this row never applies it. The frontier flag holds the coda-versus-close question open but does not test the seam, and the two verses are not one sentence, so the syntactic-continuity protection does not reach them.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY, for adjudication -- either (a) split into Isa.66.23-Isa.66.23 (the recurring-worship formula closing on its verse-final speech signature) and Isa.66.24-Isa.66.24 (the terminal judgment image), or (b) retain Isa.66.23-Isa.66.24 and supply a positive cohesion warrant that survives the verse-final closure signal at 66:23 and the scene shift at 66:24, replacing the terminal-span tiling fact. Under (a) the over-split risk of two single-verse terminal rows must be weighed, and unit_type, confidence and the rejected alternative re-open as dependent fields.

findings.claim: The book-wide 'all-flesh collocation' digit counts a skeleton substring rather than the collocation it names: it includes a site that is not the collocation and excludes an attested one.
findings.grounds: Shipped: '(sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, 6 book-wide, skeleton tier)'. Re-swept, the skeleton substring underlying "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) returns 6 verses -- Isa.22.13, Isa.40.5, Isa.49.26, Isa.66.16, Isa.66.23, Isa.66.24. The Isa.22.13 hit falls across "אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר" (oshb:Isa.22.13, byte tier), 'eat meat', where the substring spans the tail of the infinitive and the following noun and is not the all-flesh collocation at all; and the articular all-flesh site "כָּל הַבָּשָׂ֣ר" (oshb:Isa.40.6, byte tier) is excluded because its skeleton carries the article. The head word is a two-letter function word, the short-token class the hazard catalog requires word-binding for before any digit. The in-chapter digit re-verifies exactly (3 verses: Isa.66.16, Isa.66.23, Isa.66.24). Not load-bearing for either seam -- it supports the held coda question.
findings.proposed_change: Restate the book-wide digit with its object named -- either keep 6 and disclose it as a skeleton-substring census including the 'eat meat' site at 22:13, or count the collocation proper and disclose the articular site at 40:6 separately. The in-chapter digit stands as shipped.

findings.claim: The book-wide speech-signature digit is a substring census presented as a 'contiguous pair' count without naming whose frame it counts.
findings.grounds: Shipped: the pair 'stands in 53 verses book-wide and verse-final in only 5 (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier)'. Both digits re-verify at the stated skeleton tier -- 53 verses contain the substring, exactly 5 end with it, and all 5 are word-bound. But of the 53, only 42 carry a word-bound adjacency of the two tokens, and 30 of those 42 stand under the koh-amar frame that the hazard catalog role-splits (divine versus royal-messenger) before any digit is trusted; the remaining 11 of the 53 are longer verb forms in which the substring falls inside the first token. The load-bearing exclusivity digit ('verse-final in only 5') is correct, so this is a disclosure shortfall, not an arithmetic error.
findings.proposed_change: Name the swept object on the book-wide figure (e.g. disclose it as a skeleton-substring census of 53 verses, 30 of them koh-amar frames), or drop the book-wide figure and keep only the verified verse-final digit.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals files a book-unique closing image under the refrain.* namespace.
findings.grounds: The entry is 'refrain.closing_judgment_image'. The device it names is 66:24's "תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier), which the row neither claims nor sweeps as recurring anywhere in the book, while refrain.* names the recurring-formula signal class. The closure-locus test does pass -- the device stands in the row's own closing verse -- and the companion entry 'oracle_frame.recurring_worship_formula' is correctly keyed, so this is a single mis-keyed namespace.
findings.proposed_change: Re-key to a non-refrain namespace, e.g. 'oracle_frame.closing_judgment_image', or supply a recurrence sweep if a refrain relation is genuinely intended.
